title: k8s-node-provisioning-incident-breadcrumbs
content:
Summary:
- Scratchpad for the provisioning/bootstrapping incident where new nodes in pool-ml-ssd intermittently fail to register with the control plane.
- Symptoms: nodes create in cloud provider (VM visible), kubelet starts, but node object in k8s either not created or shows NotReady and then disappears after a minute.

Timeline + observations:
- 2026-02-24 10:12 UTC: autoscaler created 3 nodes (pool-ml-ssd). VMs show up in cloud console.
- 10:14: kubelet service on node-02 reports: "Failed to register node "node-02": certificate signed by unknown authority" intermittently in journal.
- 10:15: control plane events: bootstrap token expired? saw "token not found" for a few attempts. (Possible race between kubeadm and cloud-init script)
- 10:17: node object briefly created, then quickly removed by TTL controller.

Commands I ran (raw):
- Checking node list:
  kubectl get nodes -o wide --show-labels
  ---> result: node-02 not present, node-03 in NotReady for ~45s then gone

- Describe event for node object when visible:
  kubectl describe node node-03
  ---> Events:
    Type	Reason	Age	From	Message
    ----	------	---	----	-------
    Warning	FailedToRegister	2m	kubelet	Failed to register: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority

- kubelet logs (journalctl -u kubelet -f):
  Feb 24 10:13:24 node-02 kubelet[1234]: E0224 10:13:24.123456    1234 kubelet.go:1958] Error registering node: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
  Feb 24 10:13:30 node-02 kubelet[1234]: W0224 10:13:30.654321    1234 kubelet_node_status.go:456] Failed to set some node conditions: network not ready

- cloud-init / bootstrap script snippets:
  - wrote kubeadm.conf with server: https://api.internal.redwood:6443 and token from vault
  - ran: kubeadm join --config /etc/kubeadm/kubeadm.conf --v=5
  - capture: "[preflight] Running pre-flight checks
[preflight] Reading configuration from /etc/kubeadm/kubeadm.conf
[preflight] WARNING: Token appears valid but server certificate cannot be verified: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority"

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) CA mismatch between control plane certs and the kubeadm bootstrap-token CA bundle being distributed by our provisioning script. Possibly replaced CA after rotation and new images still use old CA.
2) Time skew on new VMs causing cert validation failures (NTP not configured early enough in cloud-init).
3) Vault -> bootstrap token retrieval sometimes returns stale/old token due to caching edge; token used is expired or not paired with the current CA.
4) network path/mTLS to api.internal blocked temporarily by security group rules applied after VM creation (e.g., we provision NSG rules in a second step and initial connection is disrupted).

Things tried so far:
- Re-run kubeadm join with --discovery-token-unsafe-skip-ca-verification to confirm CA is the issue:
  sudo kubeadm join --config /etc/kubeadm/kubeadm.conf --discovery-token-unsafe-skip-ca-verification
  -> node successfully registered and remained Ready (good evidence CA verification is the blocker).

- Checked system time on fresh VM:
  timedatectl status --> clock synced, NTP active (but boot logs show ntp sync happened after kubeadm join attempt)
  -> suggests time skew at early boot is plausible.

- Rotated CA locally to test: created new CA bundle and attempted join with updated certs -> works consistently for nodes using new bootstrap image. Nodes still using older image fail.

- Inspecting provisioner (k8s-autoscaler machine-template) image list + last baked date:
  - image-ml-2026-02-10 -> contains old CA certs
  - image-ml-2026-03-01 -> contains updated CA and patched cloud-init ordering
  -> nodes launched from older image correlate with failures.

Important error snippets collected:
- "x509: certificate signed by unknown authority" (kubelet)
- kubeadm preflight warning: "Token appears valid but server certificate cannot be verified"
- control plane logs: "kubelet certificate signing request rejected: CSR signer unknown" (seen in apiserver logs around same timestamps)

Next steps / TODOs (short):
- [ ] Confirm autoscaler template is still pointing at image-ml-2026-02-10 for pool-ml-ssd; update to 2026-03-01 if so. (Owner: Liam)
- [ ] Add early NTP sync step to cloud-init user-data BEFORE kubeadm join occurs (small script to block till ntp synced). (Owner: me)
- [ ] Audit Vault bootstrap token caching: check TTL and ensure we fetch latest token on each provisioning attempt. (Owner: Maya)
- [ ] Add a short-lived debug flag to provisioner to run kubeadm join with verbose logging and capture kubelet journal (for next incident).
- [ ] Create an alert for repeated "certificate signed by unknown authority" per pool (infra pager).

Notes to self / quick wins:
- Rolling forward machine image for affected pool was fastest mitigation in last incident. Do that for pool-ml-ssd to stop immediate flaps.
- Forcing CA verification skip is dangerous; only use as a debug/temporary measure to validate hypothesis.

Related links / references:
- Provisioner template: GH: ops/terraform/modules/autoscaler/machine-template.tf#L42
- Runbook draft: Confluence: infra/bootstrapping-runbook (WIP)
- Incident ticket: JIRA INFRA-4321

Questions unresolved:
- Why did some nodes from the same image succeed while others failed? (Intermittent: could be timing related with token validity window)
- Does kubeadm caching of CA certs happen locally in /etc/kubernetes/pki and sometimes contain stale certs from previous failed runs? Need to grep cloud-init logs for leftover cert files.

If I get time next: grep cloud-init logs across successful vs failed nodes and capture exact order of operations and timestamps (cloud-init-output.log, journalctl -u cloud-init). Also check Vault audit logs for token issuance times for each failed node request.

End of scratchpad.
